## Episode Thesis

Macro and geopolitics episode with Henrik von Sydow, global strategist at DNB Carnegie. He describes 2026 as a year of tectonic shifts (Venezuela, Greenland, Hormuz closure, AI transformation). He thinks the market underrates the systemic risk of large sovereign debt in the US, France and Japan, which would show up through bond yields, and overrates the systemic risk of an AI bubble. He also covers the US midterms, the dollar losing some of its safe-haven status, and Sweden's stability premium. His advice is to 'diversify madly': take some profits in concentrated US AI-tech and move toward Europe, stable cash flows and high-dividend companies. No individual stocks are recommended.
